semantics: Every term is a literal, case-insensitive substring of the row path, all terms AND-ed. FTS arm: terms of 3 or more characters are quoted phrases ANDed in one MATCH on the FTS5 trigram index (name, path); terms of 1-2 characters use path LIKE '%term%' ESCAPE '\' with backslash, percent and underscore escaped. Filters: kind equality, ext as name LIKE '%.ext' (escaped), since_mtime as mtime >= N. Baseline arm: the same semantics as plain lower-cased substring tests in Python over the files rows, no FTS table. Compared: the full unlimited set of row ids, before any ranking or limit.
limitations: Synthetic ASCII corpus with invented words, not real file trees. Ranking, bm25 and result limits are not benchmarked. Baseline scan is an in-memory Python loop over preloaded rows; FTS runs through sqlite3 from disk pages (page cache warm after warm-up). Warm-cache timings only; caches are never dropped. index_size_bytes is the size of the fts shadow tables (whole-file size if dbstat is unavailable). Non-ASCII case folding is not exercised.
